subject: wall_surface
title: Boundary stone-and-timber wall — SURFACE framing (micro-probe)
why_this_exists: Stage 1's wall subject returned 1 usable tile in 60. The diagnosis on record is that the description was OBJECT-shaped — 'a single square dungeon wall tile showing exactly two planes ... squared beams lashed twice with rope, driven iron pins, a hide strap, a salvaged plank' — and BitForge is a single-object generator, so it built the strapped timber thing it was asked for: chests, doors, sarcophagi. This file changes the FRAMING, not the register. Every construction, wear and projection clause below is carried over from subject_wall.json unchanged; what is replaced is the noun the generator is being handed. It is asked for a SURFACE, not a THING.
description: A seamless tileable wall texture, a flat repeating architectural surface filling the entire image edge to edge with no border and no background. Rough grey quarried stone laid in courses, with heavy orc-made timber pinned across it — squared beams lashed with rope, driven iron pins, a hide strap, a salvaged plank laid over an older repair. Over-built and structural: every band, strap and pin is holding something and nothing is there to be looked at. Stone and timber both rubbed smooth where shoulders and hands pass. Nothing is broken and nothing has collapsed; it is used up, not ruined. The pattern continues past all four edges of the frame.

phrase_provenance.phrase: A seamless tileable wall texture, a flat repeating architectural surface
phrase_provenance.clause: THE CHANGE UNDER TEST. Not a bible clause — a framing hypothesis, declared as such. Stage 1's wall failure is the evidence that motivates it.

phrase_provenance.phrase: filling the entire image edge to edge with no border and no background
phrase_provenance.clause: Mechanical. Stage 1's dominant wall failure was a discrete object centred on a grey field; this refuses that composition in the positive prompt as well as the negative.

phrase_provenance.phrase: The pattern continues past all four edges of the frame
phrase_provenance.clause: Mechanical, and the strongest available statement of tileability without asking for a wang set. §3's orthogonal square grid means a wall tile abuts its neighbours on all four sides.

phrase_provenance.clause: §7.4 seam 1 — 'the Boundary is mostly found stone with orc work pinned into it.' Carried over from subject_wall.json; the made/found ratio is unchanged.

arm.note: NO ARM. The micro-probe is not arm-based and carries no lighting treatment sentence and no `shading` parameter. Stage 1 established that the arms do not separate on the lighting axis, so running three of them here would spend three times the budget to re-measure a null result. The question here is framing yield, and only that.
